notes: *when he is on the watch* divides the temporal `בְּ` (*when*), its suffix (*he*) and the noun's recast predicate (*is on the watch*) under rules 52, 18 and 33; `בְּ` heads a noun rather than an infinitive, which rule 52 expressly allows.
*Or* and *his* are `added`: the Hebrew writes no conjunction in the second clause and no suffix on `אָף` (rules 14, 18).

*any* is kept with `יִקָּחֶנּוּ` as a pronoun realizing the impersonal verb's person and number (rule 17); the competing reading treats it as a supplied lexical subject on the model of `יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ` → *men shall dwell therein* and marks it `added`. No interrogative morpheme stands in the clause, so the fronted *Shall* is the verb's own.
